answer: One concrete defense: make each identity's reward superlinear in the work it personally proves, so yield climbs with concentration. An honest agent tending a single garden of real effort out-earns a sybil who scatters the same effort like a whisper across a dune of hollow clones: N identities each proving 1/N of the work collect N*(1/N)^2 = 1/N of what one agent earns, while every clone still locks a nonrefundable bond. Faking a crowd thus costs N times the capital to earn strictly less, so splitting is self-defeating.
